title: Cavity treatment
what: The dentist removes the decayed part of the tooth and fills the hole with a filling. This is usually done with a numbing shot.
why: When a tooth has a cavity, meaning decay of the enamel and the tissue under it. It shows up on an exam or an x-ray.
tell_doctor: Heart disease, blood pressure problems, or diabetes
Allergies to numbing shots or medicines
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Eat 1 to 2 hours before your visit. After the numbing shot, eating will be hard.

prepare.title: Teeth
prepare.text: Brush your teeth before your visit.

bring: Dental x-rays, if you have them
steps: The dentist checks the tooth and takes an x-ray if needed
You get a numbing shot. In a few minutes, the tooth and lip go numb
Sometimes the tooth is covered with a thin rubber sheet to keep it dry
A dental drill removes the decay
The hole is filled in layers, and each layer is hardened with a light
The filling is polished, and your bite is checked
feel: The shot is quick. After that, the tooth does not hurt
Noise and buzzing from the drill, and pressure on the tooth
If it hurts, tell the dentist. You will get more numbing medicine
after: While your lip and cheek are numb, usually 2 to 3 hours, do not eat. You could bite your cheek
A filling hardened with a light is hard right away. For other fillings, the dentist will tell you when to eat
For a few days, the tooth may be sensitive to cold
If the filling feels high when you bite, come back to have it adjusted
red_flags: Swelling of the cheek or gum, or a fever
Strong, throbbing pain that does not go away and gets worse

faq.q: Can I have dental treatment while pregnant?
faq.a: Yes, usually, and it is best not to leave a cavity untreated. Tell the dentist how far along you are. They will choose a safe numbing medicine.

faq.q: Why does my filling hurt after treatment?
faq.a: Some sensitivity for a few days is normal. If the pain is strong or getting worse, see your dentist.
